title: Dreamwars - Steampunk-themed Co-op Adventure
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7cpCkvLwQsI

Daniel (@dungeondive) says it up front: Dreamwars is not a lost gem. It's a 2017 Kickstarter whose publisher promised a revised rulebook and an FAQ, delivered neither, and then disappeared from BoardGameGeek. His shorthand for it is a simpler Arkham Horror 2nd Edition or Eldritch Horror set in a steampunk world. You get twelve heroes, including a gunslinging queen of guns, a steam-powered sentinel robot and a song-weaving cantor. Each faces one of nine nemeses, whose three factions bring their own minion pools and event decks.

He likes several ideas. The event cards stay out for three rounds, and when their suns, moons and stars line up with the nemesis sheet, rule-breaking powers switch on. Items might break and allies might desert you. Dream shards work as both consumables and currency. The adventure and outland encounter cards are atmospheric. But the branching mini-campaigns run on clocks so tight he has never won an opening scenario, and the victory conditions hang on luck. The rulebook is the bigger problem: a wall of text, keywords bolded at random, nothing said about walls, and an index without page numbers.

The one real reason to own it is the map. It looks stunning, though it's more form than function, and it's full of evocatively named places. Daniel announces he'll use it as the overworld for an upcoming solo RPG series built on Scarlet Heroes, with Folklore maps and Warhammer Quest tiles for the dungeons and his patrons helping to invent the NPCs.

----

Dreamwars is a weak game with a board Daniel loves. Have you kept a game just for its map or components, and what did you use them for?
